newsitem.title: UK: FULL TEXT - UK blocks Bass /Carlsberg-Tetley.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - UK blocks Bass /Carlsberg-Tetley.

text.p: The following is the full text of the UK Department of Trade and Industry statement blocking the proposed full acquisition of the Carlsberg-Tetley brewing company by Bass Plc.

Margaret Beckett, President of the Board of Trade and Secretary of State for Trade and Industry, has decided not to permit the acquisition by Bass PLC of Carlsberg-Tetley PLC. She has accepted the unanimous findings of the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC), contained in their report which she is publishing today, that this merger may be expected to operate against the public interest. However, she does not agree with the majority MMC view that the adverse effects of the merger can be adequately addressed by the divestment of around 1900 Bass pubs. In accordance with both the advice of the Director General of Fair Trading (DGFT) and the conclusion on remedies reached by one of the members of the MMC inquiry team (Professor Newbery), Mrs Beckett has decided that the only means of adequately dealing with the competition concerns arising from the significant shift in market power caused by this merger is to prohibit it. Mrs Beckett said: "I have noted the MMC's conclusion that the beer market has changed radically since the introduction of the Beer Orders in 1989 and continues in flux. Indeed, in the time since the MMC made its report, a further major announcement touching on the UK beer industry has been made: the proposed merger of Grand Metropolitan and Guinness. Yet despite the evolving market background I am confident that the basis for the analysis set out in the MMC's report on Bass/Carlsberg-Tetley has not been significantly changed.

"I agree with the MMC's finding that the greater concentration in brewing, the company's stronger brand portfolio and its enhanced position in wholesaling reinforced by ownership of a large tied estate would lead to significantly increased market power for Bass. I have also accepted the MMC's conclusion that the proposed merger may be expected to operate against the public interest, in that over the longer term competition for the supply of beer at the wholesale level would be reduced, wholesale prices would be higher than they would otherwise have been and there would be a consequential increase in retail prices in the on-trade. I also agree with the MMC that the existing situation whereby Bass has already acquired Allied Domecq's 50 percent stake in Carlsberg-Tetley gives rise to the same adverse effects, though to a lesser degree.

"I have given careful consideration to the majority MMC view that the adverse effects of the mergers, both existing and proposed, could be addressed by a package of undertakings involving the divestment of around 1,900 public houses by Bass.

"I am not persuaded that the divestment of 1,900 pubs would be an adequate counterweight to the substantial strengthening of Bass's position as a producer and wholesaler of beer, following the elimination of one of its three major competitors at the national level. Bass's acquisition of Carlsberg-Tetley would represent a further substantial step in the direction of concentration in an industry which has already seen the number of national brewers with tied estates fall from six to four since 1989. The merged company would also be the primary UK distributor for five of the ten top-selling beer brands in the UK. This strong portfolio would place it in a strong position to exert continuing influence over the purchasing decisions of retail outlets, even if the company's tied estate were to be substantially reduced. At the same time I am conscious that some aspects of the divestment package recommended by the MMC might be difficult to implement in practice, notably the requirement that regional brewers should

"I also considered whether there are other remedies short of prohibition which would satisfactorily deal with the adverse effects. In particular, I have considered whether I should require Bass to divest one or more beer brands as an alternative to, or in addition to, selling off parts of its tied estate. However, I agree with the MMC's unanimous conclusion that it would not be appropriate to seek undertakings from Bass on this point. It appears to me doubtful whether potential purchasers would be able to provide the substantial financial and logistical support necessary to maintain the market share of a leading brand, whilst the divestment of lesser brands would be unlikely to have a substantial impact on Bass's market power.

"I have carefully considered the possible consequences of prohibiting the merger. The MMC identified a number of options for Carlsberg-Tetley's future under these circumstances. I believe that the beer industry would be more competitive under any of these than if the merger went ahead.
"My conclusion is therefore that the proposed merger should be blocked and that the existing merger should not be allowed to continue.
"This decision is in accordance with the advice I have received from the DGFT and with the conclusion on remedies of Professor Newbery.

"I have therefore asked the DGFT to seek an undertaking from Bass that it will divest its existing 50 percent interest in Carlsberg-Tetley as well as undertakings from Bass, Carlsberg A/S and Carlsberg-Tetley that they will not proceed with the proposed merger of the UK brewing interests of Bass and Carlsberg-Tetley. If satisfactory undertakings cannot be obtained within three months I would then have to consider using my powers to make an Order to require Bass to divest its existing 50 percent shareholding in Carlsberg-Tetley and to prohibit the proposed merger of the UK brewing interests of Bass and Carlsberg-Tetley."
